meta.purpose: Real-world Japanese ATC operating practice reference for an ATC simulation game. NOT for real-world navigation.
meta.conventions: verified=true means the value was read directly in the cited source during research. verified=false means approximation, inference, enthusiast/VATSIM data, or memory that could not be confirmed. Frequencies can change at any AIRAC cycle; enthusiast frequency lists are not official.

sources.name: JCAB 管制業務処理規程 (Air Traffic Control Procedures, version republished by JAPA, Jan 2023)
sources.notes: Official Japanese ATC procedures manual. Source for radar separation (3/5 NM), wake turbulence tables (category and RECAT group), vertical separation, speed adjustment minima, simultaneous parallel ILS rules, Haneda simultaneous LDA/RNP approaches, Narita simultaneous parallel departures, and many English phraseology examples. 378 pages.

sources.name: ATCAJ/JAPA Radio Telephony Meeting Vol.025 (2021-02-22) - wake turbulence revision
sources.notes: Japan began trial ops of re-categorised wake separation on 2020-03-26; procedures amended 2020-11-05 together with ICAO PANS-ATM. Wake groups A-G are applied only at Narita and Haneda.

sources.name: ATCAJ/JAPA Radio Telephony Meeting Vol.031 (2022-01-20) - speed limits
sources.notes: Civil Aeronautics Act Art.82-2 and Enforcement Reg. Art.179: 250 kt IAS in control zones and in approach control areas at or below 10,000 ft. From 2021-12-30 the old control-zone limit below 3,000 ft (200/160 kt) was replaced by 250 kt for all aircraft.

sources.name: MLIT 関西空域における飛行経路検討について (Nov 2022)
sources.notes: KIX hourly limit was 45. A controller simulation of max hourly movements in the old airspace gave 47 (north wind) and 46 (south wind). Target about 60 per hour. Kobe limits. Itami 370/day (200 jet) and 07-21 hours.

sources.name: Hyogo Prefecture - 関西国際空港及び神戸空港の飛行経路見直し（案）に対する要望結果と対応
sources.notes: KIX north wind about 60% / south wind about 40% (5-year record). New routes: KIX departures 5,000 ft minimum over land, arrivals 4,000 ft. Arrival and departure runways swapped. New routes used 06:30-23:00 only. 23:00-06:00 traffic restricted to the Akashi/Kitan strait routes. Kobe departures capped at 3,000 ft under KIX arrivals at 4,000 ft.

RJBB.name: Kansai International (KIX)
RJBB.runwayUse: Since 2025-03-20 (new Kansai flight paths): A runway 06R/24L mainly for ARRIVALS, B runway 06L/24R mainly for DEPARTURES. From 2013 until March 2025 it was the other way round (A = departures, B = arrivals). Wind: 'north wind' ops (runway 06, NE-bound) about 60%, 'south wind' ops (runway 24) about 40% over the last 5-year record. 24-hour airport. New overland routes are used only 06:30-23:00. 23:00-06:00 (06:30) traffic uses sea routes via the Akashi and Kitan straits. At night the two runways are closed alternately for maintenance, so single-runway ops are typical overnight (the second runway removed whole-airport closures; detailed night schedule not verified).

AIP AD chart lists 121.6/121.65. Side allocation per Airband Japan.
AIP AD chart lists 118.2/118.05. Runway allocation per Airband Japan.
AIP ILS Z RWY06R chart (2012 ed.) lists KANSAI APP 120.25-125.5. Airband Japan marks 120.25 as main.
Airband Japan (sector split not stated; 124.8/120.85 noted for busy periods). 120.45/124.7 are also listed for Itami arrivals.
Airband Japan (also 120.65, 119.50 and shared radar freqs). Itami page notes 119.2 for TIGER-direction departures.

RJBB.notes: Kansai Approach (Kansai Terminal Control at KIX) provides approach/departure radar for KIX, ITM and UKB. Typical altitudes from the (old) AIP ILS Z RWY06R chart: IF ATACK 4,000 ft, FAF ZELDA 3,000 ft (GP 3.0 deg), missed approach climb to 4,000 ft to hold at AKASI. RNAV STARs (old editions) end at fixes like ALLAN/BERRY at or above 4,000 ft. CDO procedures exist (JCAB example: 'Cleared to BERRY via Runway 06L CDO Number Two, descend and maintain 4,000, comply with restrictions'). Post-2025: KIX departures 5,000 ft or above and arrivals 4,000 ft or above over land, with 1,000 ft or more vertical spacing between crossing flows over Awaji.

RJTT.name: Tokyo International (Haneda, HND)
RJTT.runwayUse: Two basic flows by wind: north wind about 60% and south wind about 40% (annual average; strongly seasonal, south wind dominant in summer). Since 2020-03-29 'new flight paths' over central Tokyo raised capacity from 80 to 90 movements per hour. South wind new routes run 15:00-19:00 (about 3 h effective). North wind new routes run 07:00-11:30 and 15:00-19:00 (about 3 h in the afternoon). 23:00-06:00 uses sea routes with a two-runway limit and the runways farthest from land. As a rule civil aircraft do not depart RWY04 or land RWY05.

configs.name: 1/2 Daytime north wind (normal)
configs.conditions: Good WX: ILS X RWY34L + HIGHWAY VISUAL RWY34R. Otherwise ILS Z RWY34L / ILS Z RWY34R.

configs.name: 3/4 Daytime north wind - new routes (07:00-11:30 and about 3 h within 15:00-19:00)
configs.conditions: Same runways, but RWY34R departures use the new northbound route (along the Arakawa river) independent of D-runway departures. About 22 departures/h from C runway.

configs.name: 5/6 Daytime south wind (normal; 06:00-15:00, 19:00-23:00)
configs.conditions: Good WX: simultaneous LDA W RWY22 / LDA W RWY23. Otherwise ILS RWY22 / ILS Z RWY23.

configs.name: 7/8 Daytime south wind - new routes over central Tokyo (about 3 h within 15:00-19:00)
configs.conditions: Good WX: simultaneous RNP RWY16L / RNP RWY16R. Otherwise ILS RWY16L / ILS RWY16R. Approx. A-runway arrivals 14/h, C-runway arrivals 30/h, B-runway (22) departures 20/h. D runway not used.

configs.conditions: Over-sea routes. NIGHT ARRIVAL STARs. Idle reverse thrust on 34L/22.

RJTT.operatingHours: 24 hours (night ops restricted to sea routes; some runway closures 23:00-06:30 for maintenance)

frequencies.unit: Tokyo Approach (Haneda, main / first contact from west)
frequencies.source: Freq listed by Airband Japan. 'Contact Tokyo Approach 119.1' appears verbatim in the JCAB procedures manual. Sector role per enthusiast blogs (unverified).

RJTT.notes: Callsigns: 'Tokyo Delivery/Ground/Tower' at Haneda; Tokyo Approach/Departure is the Tokyo terminal radar (Haneda + Narita sectors). Runway interactions (MLIT FAQ): B-arrivals crossing A runway block A departures; D-arrival go-around conflicts with A/C departures, so departures wait until the D arrival has landed; C departures and D departures conflict on northbound routes (fixed by the 2020 route). Simultaneous LDA approaches to 22/23 and simultaneous RNP approaches to 16L/16R are special procedures in the JCAB manual (Part V). New south-wind arrival paths cross central Tokyo at roughly 3,000-4,000 ft (MLIT diagrams show 3,400/3,800 ft labels near the final segments). Noise abatement: delayed-flap approach 22:00-07:00.

runways.name: B runway
runways.notes: Extension to 3,500 m (northward by 1,000 m) under construction

runways.name: C runway
runways.notes: New third runway, target completion end of March 2029

RJAA.runwayUse: Both runways are used for arrivals and departures. Since 2011-10-20 NRT has run simultaneous parallel take-off and landing ops (both runways independently mixed at peaks). The JCAB manual has a Narita-specific 'simultaneous parallel departure' procedure with WAM monitoring, a DNTZ 610 m wide (34L/34R: from 600 m past the 34L start of roll to 14 NM; 16R/16L: to 21 NM) and RNAV initial waypoint check in the take-off clearance. North vs south wind split not found in an official source.

configs.conditions: Mixed mode. Southbound departures may delay their turn until 6,000 ft and clear of noise areas (about 13 km for A, 10 km for B) when congested.

Narita arrivals/departures are worked by Tokyo Approach/Departure Narita sectors (Tokyo terminal control). The JCAB example 'Resume own navigation, 15 miles northwest of PAPAS, turn left heading 160 to intercept Narita VOR 137 Radial' is from the manual.

RJOO.name: Osaka International (Itami, ITM)

runways.name: B runway
runways.use: Large jets (B777/767/787/A320 etc.). Only runway with ILS (32L).

RJOO.runwayUse: Normally '32 operation': arrivals from the south on ILS 32L (jets) and departures northwest on 32L (jets) / 32R (small aircraft). '14 operation' (SE-bound) is rare, reportedly about 3% (enthusiast source). In 14 ops arrivals fly the ILS 32L course and then break right, circling to land 14R/14L (the 'Itami curve').

RJBE.runwayUse: Single runway 09/27. Operating hours 07:00-23:00 (extended from 22:00 in March 2020). Under the 2025 Kansai route revision, Kobe departures crossing under KIX arrivals are capped at 3,000 ft (KIX arrivals 4,000 ft) near the Akashi strait/Awaji, with the altitude-restriction points set over the sea.

RJBE.notes: UKB is inside the Kansai terminal airspace; arrivals/departures are radar-controlled by Kansai Approach/Radar.

acc.notes: Airspace reorganisation (上下分離, vertical split): the en-route airspace is split at 33,500 ft. Fukuoka ACC handles all high-altitude (above 33,500 ft) and oceanic airspace. Tokyo ACC (Tokorozawa) handles low-altitude airspace in east Japan (Hokkaido to Kanto, part of Tokai, and southern Kinki incl. the Kii Peninsula). Kobe ACC handles low-altitude airspace in west Japan (west of Hokuriku/Kamikochi, excluding the Kii Peninsula), including the former Naha area. Timeline: Naha ACC abolished 2018 (moved to Kobe). West Japan split started FY2022. East Japan split from 2023, completed March 2025. Sapporo ACC airspace split in March 2024 (upper to Fukuoka), lower moved to Tokyo ACC in October 2024, and Sapporo ACC abolished. So there are now 3 ACCs: Tokyo (15-17 sectors), Kobe (11), Fukuoka (22). The Kansai lower en-route airspace (feeding KIX/ITM/UKB) is Kobe ACC (sector N44 'southern Gifu to Kansai'). Arrivals from the south/east over the Kii Peninsula are in Tokyo ACC lower airspace. Kanto lower airspace is Tokyo ACC. Callsign is '<Tokyo/Kobe/Fukuoka> Control'. Below the terminal areas: Tokyo Approach/Departure (Haneda+Narita), Kansai Approach/Departure (KIX+ITM+UKB).

terminal.rule: Both targets from airport surveillance radar (ASR) within 40 NM of the radar site (not supplementary targets), or from airport WAM.
terminal.source: JCAB 管制業務処理規程 (IV)6(4)a

enroute.source: JCAB 管制業務処理規程 (IV)6(4)a(b)

boundaryBuffer.value: 1.5 NM (3 NM-radar) / 2.5 NM (5 NM-radar) from an adjacent sector boundary when the neighbour also applies radar separation; 3/5 NM if not

arrivalVsDeparture.value: 2 NM radar separation between an arrival and a departure, and the full radar minimum within 1 minute after take-off

initialDepartureSpacing.value: Successive departures (same runway, or parallels under 760 m apart) on routes diverging at least 15 deg: at least 1 NM radar separation at the divergence point, if the follower will be radar-identified within 1 NM of the runway end. Simultaneous take-off allowed from parallels 760 m or more apart with routes diverging at least 15 deg.

vertical.value: 1,000 ft up to FL290; 2,000 ft above FL290; 1,000 ft between RVSM-approved aircraft in RVSM airspace (FL290-FL410); 2,000 ft RVSM vs non-RVSM. 500 ft between IFR and VFR in PCA (special control airspace).
vertical.source: JCAB 管制業務処理規程 (II)2(2)a

wakeTurbulenceRadar.categoryNotes: ICAO categories J (Super), H, M, L. The J>H value was reduced in the 2020 revision. Applies when the follower is at the same altitude or less than 1,000 ft below and in trail, or when using the same runway or parallels under 760 m apart (arrivals until the leader crosses the threshold, unless visual approach).
wakeTurbulenceRadar.groupNotes: Wake groups A-G (ICAO PANS-ATM 2020, RECAT-EU/1.5-style) are used in Japan only at Narita and Haneda (requires a system that shows the group on the controller display). Trial began 2020-03-26, formal from 2020-11-05. Pairs not listed fall back to the radar minimum (3 NM in terminal). Since the revision 'Heavy'/'Super' must be appended to callsigns of category H/J aircraft.
wakeTurbulenceRadar.source: JCAB 管制業務処理規程 (IV)6(4)b ; ATCAJ R/T Meeting Vol.025

wakeTurbulenceDepartureTime.notes: Time from the leader starting its take-off roll to take-off clearance for the follower (same direction), unless the terminal radar wake distances are applied.
wakeTurbulenceDepartureTime.source: JCAB 管制業務処理規程 (III)3(2)b

runway.value: A following departure may not start its roll until the preceding departure has crossed the runway end or turned away, or the preceding arrival has vacated (crossed the holding-position marking, or cleared the runway edge if it will cross without delay).
runway.source: JCAB 管制業務処理規程 (III)3(2)a

parallelRunways.simultaneousParallelILS: Allowed when centrelines are at least 1,310 m (4,300 ft) apart, straight-in only, missed approach paths diverging at least 30 deg, NTZ displayed and monitored by a separate controller per localizer, with tower-frequency override. 3 NM radar or 1,000 ft vertical until the higher aircraft joins the glide path. Join the localizer at least 2 NM outside the approach gate, intercept angle optimum 20 deg / max 30 deg. ATIS/ATC: 'SIMULTANEOUS PARALLEL ILS APPROACHES TO RUNWAY 34 LEFT AND RIGHT ARE IN PROGRESS'.
parallelRunways.simultaneousTakeoffLanding: Landing on one parallel and departing the other is allowed if the departure path diverges at least 30 deg from the missed approach path: A-type parallels 760 m or more apart, B-type parallels 1,310 m or more apart.
parallelRunways.HND: Special procedures: simultaneous LDA approaches RWY22/RWY23 (3 NM or 1,000 ft until the RWY22 FAF, NTZ 610 m wide) and simultaneous RNP RWY16L/16R approaches (no radar separation between the two streams).
parallelRunways.NRT: Simultaneous parallel departures with Narita WAM and DNTZ. Take-off clearance prefixed 'RNAV to <first waypoint>'. Simultaneous parallel landing/take-off since 2011.
parallelRunways.source: JCAB 管制業務処理規程 (IV)8-4, (IV)6(9), Part V

transitionAltitude.notes: Altitudes of 14,000 ft and above are normally expressed as flight levels; QNH is used up to 13,000 ft in practice (14,000 ft is called FL140).
transitionAltitude.source: squawk.id (quoting 管制方式基準); search summary of Japanese sources

transitionLevel.value: FL140 when QNH is 29.92 inHg or higher; FL150 for 29.91-28.92; FL160 for 28.91-27.92 (lowest usable FL table)
transitionLevel.notes: Some Japanese sources simply state 'TL normally FL150'.

qnhUnits.value: inHg, read as four digits, e.g. 'QNH 2984', 'QNH3002'
qnhUnits.notes: A Japan-specific item that a game should reproduce. hPa is not used in ATC instructions.
qnhUnits.source: JCAB manual phraseology examples ('Japanair 91, runway16L, QNH 2984')

typicalApproachAltitudes.value: KIX ILS Z RWY06R (old chart): IF 4,000 ft, FAF 3,000 ft, GP 3.0 deg. KIX new arrival restriction 4,000 ft over land. HND final approach altitudes typically 3,000-4,000 ft on the base/final legs (new route diagrams show 3,000-5,000 ft). JCAB examples: 'Fly heading 090 vector to final approach course, maintain 6,000', 'descend via STAR to altitude 2,000'.
typicalApproachAltitudes.source: AIP chart (yinlei RJBB, 2012 ed.), MLIT HND diagrams, JCAB manual. Treat as approximate for gameplay.

legalLimit.value: 250 kt IAS in control zones and in approach control areas at or below 10,000 ft
legalLimit.notes: Not a blanket 'below 10,000 ft everywhere' rule; it applies in 管制圏 + 進入管制区 at or below 10,000 ft. The old 200 kt (turbine) / 160 kt (piston) limit at or below 3,000 ft in control zones was abolished on 2021-12-30. ATC may authorise more only for hijack/medical emergencies ('maintain 300kts or less'). Pilots may exceed for safety and should advise, e.g. 'our climb speed 280kts due to performance'.
legalLimit.source: ATCAJ R/T Meeting Vol.031 ; 航空法施行規則 第179条

minimumAssignableSpeeds.minimumCleanSpeedNote: Jet minimum clean speed is usually about 220 kt below FL150
minimumAssignableSpeeds.source: JCAB 管制業務処理規程 (IV)9(5)

otherRules.value: IAS in multiples of 10 kt; Mach (0.01 steps) may be used at FL250 and above. No specific-speed assignment on RF legs. For RNP/RNP AR approaches, do not assign speeds that would exceed 210 kt at procedure waypoints. Speed control ends automatically on hold, 'descend via STAR', approach clearance, or 5 NM from touchdown on a radar approach. Phrases: 'RESUME PUBLISHED SPEED' / 'RESUME NORMAL SPEED'.

typicalApproachProfile.value: Typical game profile: 250 kt below 10,000 ft, 210-220 kt on downwind/intermediate, 180 kt on base/intercept, 160 kt to 5 NM final (JCAB example: 'Cleared for ILS runway 34L approach, maintain 160 knots until 5 miles on final'). Holding/missed-approach legs at KIX charted MAX 230 KIAS.
typicalApproachProfile.source: 160 kt to 5 NM example verified in the JCAB manual. 210/180 steps are common practice consistent with the 210/170 minima but not a published Japanese standard.

phraseology.source: JCAB manual examples; ATCAJ R/T Meeting Vol.025

classes.value: Class A: PCA A (特別管制空域A), en-route control areas at or above FL290, oceanic at or above 20,000 ft. Class B/C: PCA B/C (special control airspace around major airports; VFR needs ATC permission - never in PCA A, in B only if no impact on all traffic, in C only if no impact on IFR). Class D: control zones (管制圏, typically about 5 NM radius / 3,000 ft AGL). Class E: approach control areas (進入管制区), information zones and other controlled airspace. Class G: uncontrolled. TCAs (terminal control areas) provide radar advisory to VFR.
classes.source: JCAB manual (PCA A/B/C VFR rules - verified); VATJPN class document and search summary (class mapping - partly verified; VATJPN says the major-airport PCAs are Class C)

kansai.value: Kansai Approach (radar at KIX) controls the terminal airspace that contains KIX, ITM and UKB. KIX is on the SE shore of Osaka Bay, UKB on the north shore (Kobe), ITM inland north of Osaka. KIX arrivals and departures are kept largely over Osaka Bay and Awaji Island. Since 2025 KIX traffic flies over Awaji Island (departures 5,000 ft or above, arrivals 4,000 ft or above over land). Kobe departures crossing under KIX arrivals are capped at 3,000 ft near the Akashi strait. Congestion near the Akashi strait was a key driver of the 2025 redesign. Itami arrivals come from the south over Osaka city on ILS 32L. Night (23:00-06:00) KIX traffic must use the Akashi or Kitan (Tomogashima) straits. Old STARs show gates at MAYAH (cross at 4,000 ft) via AKASI/LILAC/TOMO arrivals. Approximate approach area: roughly 40-50 NM around Osaka Bay (approximation, not verified).
kansai.source: Hyogo doc ; MLIT 2022 ; AIP old STAR charts (lateral extent approximate)

tokyo.value: Tokyo Approach/Departure (Tokyo terminal control) covers Haneda and Narita (Narita sectors use separate frequencies). Haneda flows mostly over Tokyo Bay, except the 2020 new routes over central Tokyo (south wind arrivals to 16L/16R) and the north wind RWY34R northbound departure along the Arakawa. Arrivals from the south/west via OSHIMA/AKSEL/AROSA STARs and from the north/east via GODIN/POLIX (per VATSIM STAR table). Approximate terminal area: about 50 NM around Haneda (approximation).
tokyo.source: MLIT HND docs (routes verified); squawk.id (STAR names); lateral extent approximate

yokota.value: Yokota RAPCON airspace (横田進入管制区) is controlled by the US Air Force (JASDF controllers co-located since 2007). It covers airspace over 10 prefectures: Tokyo (west), Saitama, Gunma, Tochigi, Fukushima, Niigata, Nagano, Yamanashi, Shizuoka, Kanagawa. Its upper limit is stepped from about 12,000 ft up to about 23,000 ft (7,000 m). Partial returns: about 10% in 1992 and about 20% in September 2008 for Haneda capacity. IFR flights need prior permission. Effect on HND: westbound departures from Haneda first head east/south over Tokyo Bay and then climb to cross above the Yokota block (or route south around it). Arrivals from the west are funnelled south of it (via Oshima). Since 2020, part of the new HND arrival paths passes through Yokota airspace temporarily under Japanese control.
yokota.source: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/横田空域 (extent, altitude, returns, 2020 note). HND routing effect is general knowledge (verified=false for that clause).

enrouteSplit.value: Fukuoka ACC above 33,500 ft. Tokyo/Kobe ACC at or below 33,500 ft (lower).

notes: Key gaps: (1) KIX night runway schedule and the exact post-2025 STAR/approach charts were not obtained (the AIP charts found were 2009-2012 editions). (2) The NRT north/south wind split and per-runway arr/dep preference were not found officially. (3) Tokyo ACC sector-to-area mapping after the 2025 reorganisation is not published in the sources found; former-sector links are inference. (4) Most tower/ground/approach frequencies come from enthusiast lists (Airband Japan), except the KIX ones on the AIP AD chart and the frequencies quoted in JCAB examples (Tokyo Approach 119.1, Narita Ground 121.95, Ground 121.7). (5) HND 23:00-06:00 runway use is from VATSIM Japan commentary. (6) The airspace class mapping (B vs C for PCAs) and the lateral extents of the terminal areas are approximate. (7) The 'Osaka Tower' callsign for Itami is not verified. Corrections to the original brief: Sapporo ACC no longer exists (abolished Oct 2024), and the 250 kt rule applies only in control zones and approach control areas at or below 10,000 ft. The transition altitude is 14,000 ft and the transition level is FL140 (FL150/160 when QNH is low).
